# #6727 — notes

## Verdict in one line

The capability is still absent on `main`. The DXIL opcodes exist, are fully
documented and are emitted by DXC's own DXBC-to-DXIL converter; nothing in the
HLSL front end can reach them, in any release from v1.4.1907 to v1.9.2607.

Ground truth: `main-debug`, Debug build, `--version` reports
`1.9.0.5433 (triage, ab5400907)`. That commit is fork-local and resolves
nowhere public; the identical upstream source is `13730886e`, which is what the
draft cites.

## What was measured

### 1. Ground-truth compile (`out-main-debug.txt`)

`dxc -T cs_6_0 -E main repro.hlsl`, exit 0. The repro asks for both outputs of a
32x32 multiply and for the quotient and remainder of one operand pair. DXIL:

```
;       64-Bit integer
  %8 = mul nuw i64 %7, %6
  %9 = lshr i64 %8, 32
  %10 = trunc i64 %9 to i32
  %11 = trunc i64 %8 to i32
  %12 = udiv i32 %4, %5
  %13 = urem i32 %4, %5
```

The `64-Bit integer` line is the shader's feature-requirement banner: obtaining
the high half at all pulls in the optional feature.

Both halves of the request behave exactly as `expected.md` predicted before the
run: the high 32 bits cost a widening to 64-bit and the `64-Bit integer`
feature flag — the precise cost `tex3d` said intrinsics would avoid — and the
divide and the remainder stay as two independent instructions. No
`dx.op.binaryWithTwoOuts` call anywhere.

### 2. The DXIL opcodes exist and are unreachable only from HLSL

| where | what it says |
| --- | --- |
| `include/dxc/DXIL/DxilConstants.h:697,709,711` | `IMul = 41`, `UDiv = 43`, `UMul = 42` |
| `lib/DXIL/DxilOperations.cpp:390-415` | all three in op class `BinaryWithTwoOuts`, `dx.op` name `binaryWithTwoOuts`, overload `i`, `ReadNone`; return type `p2I32` (a two-`i32` struct) |
| `docs/DXIL.rst:2729,3005,3038` | full semantics, including "Either destQUOT or destREM may be specified as NULL" |
| `utils/hct/hctdb.py:1945-1959` | the generator entry; result param type `twoi32` |
| `projects/dxilconv/.../DxbcConverter.cpp:2651-2657` | the **only** in-tree emitter — the DXBC-to-DXIL converter |
| `utils/hct/gen_intrin_main.txt` | **no** intrinsic maps to any of them |

`git grep -n "OpCode::UMul\|OpCode::IMul\|OpCode::UDiv"` over the whole tree
returns the definitions, the `DxilInstructions.h` accessors, and dxilconv.

**One trap for whoever implements this.** `lib/HLSL/HLOperationLower.cpp:7860`
reads

```cpp
{IntrinsicOp::IOP_umul, TranslateMul, DXIL::OpCode::UMul},
```

which looks like the op is already wired up. It is not: `IOP_umul` is the
unsigned overload of HLSL's `mul()` (matrix/vector multiply), and
`TranslateMul` (`HLOperationLower.cpp:3185`) never reads its `opcode`
parameter — it branches on `IOP` to choose `IMad`/`UMad` for the dot expansion
and otherwise calls `Builder.CreateMul`. So `DXIL::OpCode::UMul` appears in the
HLSL lowering table and is dead.

### 3. FXC reaches the two-output instruction from the same HLSL

`manual-case-fxc-vs-dxc.txt`, generated by `make-manual-cases.py` (which echoes
each argv with `subprocess.list2cmdline`, so the commands in it are the commands
that ran):

| source | FXC `cs_5_0` (DXBC) | DXC `cs_6_0` (DXIL) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `a / b` and `a % b` | `udiv r0.x, r1.x, r0.x, r0.y` — one instruction, both results | `udiv i32` + `urem i32` |
| `a * b` | `imul null, r1.y, r0.y, r0.x` — the two-output instruction with the high half discarded into `null` | `mul i32` |

The second row is the more telling one: in DXBC the two-output form *is* the
multiply instruction, and HLSL has only ever been able to take the low half.
This is the direct evidence behind the issue's "part of the shader models since
4.0", and behind proposing `fxc-disagrees`.

### 4. The SPIR-V path has the same gap (`variant-spirv-main-debug.txt`)

`-spirv` on the repro emits `OpCapability Int64`, a 64-bit `OpIMul` +
`OpShiftRightLogical`, and separate `OpUDiv`/`OpUMod`. No `OpUMulExtended` —
the SPIR-V op behind the GLSL `umulExtended` that `jstoecker` cited. DXC's
SPIR-V backend knows the opcode only as an entry in an instruction-kind switch
(`tools/clang/lib/SPIRV/SpirvInstruction.cpp:169`); nothing generates it. So a
new intrinsic would need a lowering in both backends, but it would map onto an
existing SPIR-V instruction rather than an emulation.

### 5. History (`bisect --linear`, 20 stable releases)

All 20 catalog releases from v1.4.1907 (2019-07) to v1.9.2607 score `repro`:
each compiles the shader successfully and none emits the op. No invalid probes
— v1.4.1907, the oldest, already accepts `uint64_t` in `cs_6_0` and produces
byte-for-byte the same shape (`mul nuw i64`, `udiv i32`, `urem i32`).

`v1.5.2003` was also run by hand (`out-v1.5.2003.txt`, `repro`), but it is a
prerelease and the issue does not explicitly name it. Under the standing policy
it is supplemental evidence, not part of the history population or boundary.

`always-repro'd` here means **never implemented in any tested stable release**,
not "regressed long ago".

## The predicate and its controls

`match.json` = `all_of[ regex "define void @main\(\)", regex "udiv i32",
regex "urem i32", not_regex "binaryWithTwoOuts" ]`.

The symptom is an absence, which is the predicate shape with the two documented
failure modes, so each control flips exactly one clause
(`manual-case-clause-table.txt`):

| control | flips | proves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `control-parse-error.hlsl` (`--expect no-match`) | entry-point anchor | a compile that emits no DXIL satisfies the absence clause for free; under a bare `not_regex` it would have scored as a textbook reproduction |
| `control-no-divide.hlsl` (`--expect no-match`) | `udiv`/`urem` anchors | the predicate is not vacuously true of any clean compile |
| `control-token-visible.hlsl` (`--expect no-match`) | `binaryWithTwoOuts` | the absence clause is falsifiable: with `-Zi -Qembed_debug` the token reaches the output via `!dx.source.contents` and the predicate stops matching |
| `control-fxc-divrem.hlsl` (`--expect match`) | nothing | the FXC-comparable source behaves identically on the DXC side, so the FXC/DXC comparison is like-for-like |

**What the predicate cannot do.** It cannot prove "no HLSL construct anywhere
reaches these ops" — no predicate over one shader can. That claim rests on
section 2: the intrinsic table has no entry, and the only emitter in the tree is
the DXBC converter.

## Thread state, checked rather than assumed

* No maintainer has rejected the request. `llvm-beanz` (2023-07-13) tagged it a
  feature request needing prioritisation and a spec; `tex3d` established the same
  day that the shader5x HLK test already covers these ops in DXIL via
  translation, so no shader-model revision is needed; `damyanp` (2024-06-26)
  confirmed no SM change and asked `davidcook-msft` to establish priority.
* Nothing has moved since. A search of `microsoft/hlsl-specs` for `umul`,
  `mulhi`, `UMulExtended`, `IMul` and `umulExtended` returns 0 issues/PRs, so the
  "spec it out" step has not started in that repo.
* `microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler#4612` ("Does DXC support `__umulhi`?") was
  closed into this issue on 2023-07-13 — a second, independent user asking for
  the same thing.
* **`llvm/llvm-project#128638`** (open, `farzonl`, 2025-02-25, `backend:DirectX`)
  tracks lowering `USubb`/`IMul`/`UMul`/`UDiv` in the successor DirectX backend.
  It reaches the same conclusion this triage measured — "there still is no HLSL
  intrinsic yet for most of these ... these DXIL Ops exist primarily to convert
  DXBC to DXIL" — and proposes mapping `UMul`→`umul_with_overflow`,
  `IMul`→`smul_with_overflow`, `USubb`→`usub_with_overflow`, with `UDiv` TBD. It
  is explicitly waiting on the DXC-side language decision.

## Assessment

* status `repros` — for a feature request, the capability is still absent.
* repro quality `agent-constructed` — the issue has no shader or command line,
  because it is a design request.
* history `always-repro'd` — never implemented, over the full bisectable range.
* confidence `high` — the compiler measurement, the source inspection and the
  FXC contrast all agree, and an independent 2025 LLVM issue reaches the same
  reading.
* suggested action `enhancement-not-bug` — keep open; the next step is the
  language decision `llvm-beanz` named, not a compiler fix.

Not `text-stale`: the body's claim ("part of the shader models since 4.0 ... HLSL
has never explicitly exposed these") is exactly what the compiler still does, and
no comment left standing in the thread contradicts it.

## Labels

Propose adding `fxc-disagrees` — "Issues tracking differences between FXC and
DXC" — on the strength of section 3, which is a measured difference rather than
an inference. Keep `enhancement` and `high-impact`; nothing in the thread or the
evidence argues against either.

Considered and rejected: `hlsl-next` would read as deferring the work to a
future language version, which contradicts `tex3d`'s and `damyanp`'s position
that it can be enabled retrospectively for older shader models; `hlk-gap` is
wrong because `tex3d` says the shader5x HLK test already covers these ops;
`validation` means DXIL validation specifically. `ML Foundations` ("Issues
enabling ML hardware features") is arguable — the two in-thread motivations are
Philox PRNG for ML frameworks and DirectML's int64 emulation — but whether that
label is a routing signal or a workstream tag is not something this triage can
verify, so it is left to a maintainer rather than proposed.
